caption:
A store in Tokyo that only sells black t-shirts… but it goes deeper than that.

Not only @000t_macqlo offer a curated selection of premium black tees from around the world—but they also do something wild:
They can dye your old clothes jet black using a century-old Japanese dyeing technique from Kyoto.

The owner, Natsume-san, is the same guy behind the store that only sells white T-shirts (I made a video about that store too, go find it @breakthru.ig).
His attention to detail and love for simplicity makes this place feel more like a gallery than a shop.

Got a faded or stained piece you love? This place might just bring it back to life—darker, cooler, and better than ever.

Enjoyed the discovery? Follow @breakthru.ig for more!".

caption:
Tucked away in the Asakusa underground shopping arcade, Fukuchan is a yakisoba spot that has been serving locals for decades. Its retro Showa-era atmosphere and sizzling teppan grill evoke a sense of nostalgia, making it a beloved spot for both residents and visitors. ￼

Founded in 1963, Fukuchan gained international recognition as one of the filming locations for Wim Wenders’ 2023 film Perfect Days. In the movie, Hirayama frequents this eatery, highlighting its authentic charm and significance in Tokyo’s culinary landscape. ￼ ￼

The menu is straightforward yet satisfying, featuring generous portions of yakisoba cooked on a large iron plate at the storefront. Fukuchan’s unpretentious setting and flavorful dishes offer a glimpse into Tokyo’s everyday life, making it a worthwhile stop for those seeking an authentic dining experience.
